title: T1-T12 coupled (secondary) ROM with intact rib cage (Liebsch 2020 FB, intact condition)

quantity.name: coupled ROM
quantity.definition: secondary (out-of-plane) T1-T12 range of motion during primary loading at +/-5 Nm; median with min/max; negative = inverse motion. LB->AR is ipsilateral, AR->LB contralateral (per figure legends)

source.authors: Liebsch C, Kocak T, Aleinikov V, Kerimbayev T, Akshulakov S, Jansen JU, Vogt M, Wilke HJ
source.sample: 6 fresh-frozen human C7-L1 thoracic spines with intact rib cage (anatomy dept. Aachen)

protocol.summary: C7-L1 with intact rib cage, C7 and L1 potted; pure moments +/-5 Nm FE/LB/AR, 1 deg/s, 3.5 cycles (3rd evaluated), no preload. Only the un-instrumented intact condition (step 1) is extracted; steps 2-5 (T6 vertebral body replacement with unilateral/bilateral approach, long T4-T8 or short T5-T7 pedicle-screw instrumentation) are fe_instrumented and not extracted.
how_to_simulate: Fix L1, apply pure moments +/-5 Nm to C7 in FE, LB, AR, no preload
Model full rib cage (sternum, costal cartilage, ribs, costovertebral joints; no intercostal muscles); use osteoporotic bone properties if relevant
Report total T1-T12 rotation (full range) in the primary plane and coupled planes at peak moment
protocol.notes: Values digitised from Figs 3-5 (median bars with min-max whiskers, n=6). Old, osteoporotic donors (63-99 y) - independent of the Liebsch 2017 and 2018-2020 specimen pools by age/sex/source (Aachen, 2018).

data.note: grey NZ portion of this coupled bar ~5.8 deg

extraction.uncertainty: +/-0.4 deg; near-zero bars only resolvable to +/-0.4 deg
extraction.check_notes: Pixel-scanned at 200 dpi (5.1-5.2 px/deg); intact primary medians agree with red reference line; re-scanned adjacent columns for 2 bars (same pixel rows).

pass_rule.rule: model within [min,max] of specimens (median as target)

ribcage.intact_structures: entire rib cage with sternum, costal cartilage, ribs and costovertebral joints; muscles incl. intercostal muscles removed

loading.device: spine tester (Wilke 1994) + optical tracking, 3 markers per vertebra
